East of 6th Street and the abandoned right of way of the
North Shore Railroad, the corridor would cross two intermittent streams
which flow together into the Metropolitan Sewerage Commisson concrete
drainage ditch system. The land is agricultural in usage but is zoned
for industrial use and held by the City of Milwaukee. Between 6th
and 3rd Streets this corridor would sever portions of the City of Milwaukee's
land bank area and require several newly constructed industrial buildings.
Presently the north-south property lines are approximately 1/2 mile
apart and abut Edgerton Avenue as well as Grange Avenue. East of 3rd
Street commercial properties abut both 3rd Street and Howell Avenue.
At Howell Avenue the corridor would displace two motels and a business
complex.
According to airport officials the east end of this corridor, before it crosses Howell Avenue, would be directly under the landing path of the southwest runway located north of the Air Terminal. The Federal Aviation Administration glide slope-highway clearance requirements would necessitate constructing the freeway under Howell Avenue. This corridor would therefore conflict with present plans for the air terminal expansion program in relocating passenger loading and ticket operations to the second level of the air terminal.
The length of Corridor #2 from existing I-94 to a point east of Howell Avenue would be 1.39 miles.
It is estimated that a freeway facility in this corridor would have originally displaced 200 people from 54 housing units. There would also be 6 comercial parcels displaced.
